question: Atlassian senior software engineer low level design (code design) round. A cinema has a **single screen**. It opens around **10 am**, and the last show can run until **11 pm**. If a movie ends at 12 pm, the next one can start **exactly at 12 pm**. Screenings carry a movie name, start time and duration. Implement `canSchedule(Movie movie, CurrentMovieSchedule schedule)` returning whether the movie can be put into the schedule with **no overlaps**, with the start time not before 10 am and not after 11 pm. **Follow-ups:** support **replacing** a movie in the schedule, and handle the case where each movie has an associated **revenue**.
lookingFor: Interval overlap logic with correct boundary handling.
Reasoning about replace and optimisation extensions (weighted scheduling).
Clear communication of assumptions about ambiguous times.
answer:
**Clarify the ambiguity.** The report says the last show can run up to 11 pm and start times cannot be after 11 pm. Ask whether 11 pm bounds the **start** or the **end**; state your assumption and keep the bounds in constants. The check below assumes the movie must start at or after open and finish by close.

**Core check.** Here the movie comes with a proposed start time. Two intervals `[s1, e1)` and `[s2, e2)` overlap exactly when `s1 < e2 and s2 < e1`; using half-open intervals makes back-to-back screenings legal. So:

```
canSchedule(movie, schedule):
    s, e = movie.start, movie.start + movie.duration
    if s < OPEN or e > CLOSE: return false
    for x in schedule.screenings:
        if s < x.end and x.start < e: return false
    return true
```

O(n) per query. If the schedule is kept sorted by start, binary search for the neighbouring screenings and check only the previous end and next start: O(log n).

**Follow-up 1: replace a movie.** Replacing screening `X` with new movie `M` means checking `M` against all screenings **except** `X`. Implement `canReplace(old, new, schedule)` by skipping `old` in the loop (or building a temporary list). Do the check first and mutate only on success, so a failed replace leaves the schedule unchanged. A new movie with different duration at the same start time is the common case.

**Follow-up 2: revenue.** This can mean two things; ask. (a) When there is a conflict, replace conflicting screenings only if the new movie's revenue exceeds the total revenue of those it would displace: collect conflicting screenings and compare sums. (b) Maximise total revenue over a set of candidate movies with fixed start times: this is **weighted interval scheduling**, solved by sorting by end time and dynamic programming with binary search for the last compatible interval, O(n log n).

**Design.** Keep `Screening` immutable with `start`, `end`; a `Schedule` class owning the list and exposing `canSchedule`, `add`, `replace`; make open and close configurable. Test boundaries: exactly at 10:00, ending exactly at 23:00, touching neighbours.
followUps: Why use half-open intervals for the overlap test?
How would the DP for revenue maximisation work?
How would you make the schedule safe for concurrent booking?
How would you extend this to several screens?
